name: Create residents table with identity, contact and KYC fields
w: Residents are the second core entity after beds. The record must hold enough identity detail for police verification style checks without becoming a form that nobody fills in correctly.
ac: residents has hostel_id, full_name, phone, alt_phone, email, gender, dob, id_proof_type, id_proof_number, guardian_name, guardian_phone, permanent_address, joining_date, status and notes
RLS enabled with the hostel-scoped pattern
Indexes exist on hostel_id plus phone and on full_name for search
Status constrained to active, notice, vacated and blocked
out: No PAN, Aadhaar vault or police verification document workflow.

name: Implement resident registration form with validation
w: Front-desk staff register residents in a hurry, often on a phone. Server-side validation is the only thing preventing inconsistent data that later breaks fee generation.
ac: Indian mobile number format enforced for phone and guardian phone
Date of birth sanity-checked to a plausible age range with a clear message
Required fields enforced on the server, not just in the browser
Invalid submissions never reach the database
Successful registration redirects to the resident profile
out: No bulk import of existing residents in the MVP.

name: Prevent duplicate resident records within a hostel
w: Duplicate residents split fee history across two records and make outstanding balances impossible to trust, which is the exact thing the product is sold on.
ac: Duplicate detection on normalised phone number
Duplicate detection on id_proof_type plus id_proof_number
On a match the UI offers to open the existing record instead of inserting
A database-level unique constraint backs the UI check
An integration test proves the constraint rejects a duplicate insert

name: Build resident list with search and status filters
w: Search is the most used feature in any hostel back office. Owners look residents up by name or by the phone number the resident called from.
ac: Search matches name, phone and room
Filters by resident status and by room
Result count is displayed
Remains responsive with 2000 residents using indexed, paginated queries
No results from another hostel can appear
out: No saved filter presets or CSV export.

name: Build resident profile detail page
w: This page is the single view of a resident: who they are, where they sleep and what they owe. It is where staff answer almost every phone call from a resident or parent.
ac: Shows personal and contact details plus KYC reference
Shows current room and bed, or an explicit not-allocated state
Shows allocation history with dates
Shows fee history and current outstanding balance
Action entry points for allocate, record payment and vacate are present and permission-guarded
out: No downloadable resident statement in the MVP.

name: Implement resident status lifecycle
w: Residents move through notice and vacate states, and each transition has different billing consequences. Modelling it explicitly stops vacated residents from being billed.
ac: Transitions supported: active to notice, notice to vacated, plus blocked
Invalid transitions are rejected server-side
Status changes are timestamped with the actor
Vacated residents are excluded from active occupancy counts but remain searchable
A vacated resident cannot be allocated to a bed without being reactivated
out: No notice-period length rules or refund calculation in the MVP.

name: Add ID proof upload via Supabase Storage
w: ID proof copies are expected during admission, but they are also the most sensitive data the product will hold, so they must be stored privately and scoped per hostel from the start.
ac: Private bucket with a hostel-scoped object path
Access only through short-lived signed URLs
File type and size validated (PDF, JPG or PNG, 5 MB maximum)
A user from another hostel cannot fetch the file even with a guessed path
Storage policies are committed as SQL alongside table policies
out: No automatic OCR extraction of ID data in the MVP.
